records.description: The Organization of American States (OAS) Academic Program, in partnership with Universidad de los Andes, offers a scholarship to study the 2GL (Global Data Literacy) online course delivered by the UDD dLab. The scholarship covers part of the course fee, and applications are submitted through the form on the OAS Academic Program portion of the OAS website. Selection is based on a résumé and one letter of recommendation, and the announcement specifies that the programme covers approximately 83 percent of the total course cost.

applicant_utility.description: This is a short online course scholarship, not degree funding: it offsets USD 3,400 of a USD 3,800 course for the 2GL (Global Data Literacy) course run by the UDD dLab at Universidad de los Andes. The file you send in is small - essentially a résumé and one letter of recommendation - so the competitive difference comes from how sharply those two documents speak to data literacy work you have already done.
eligibility_tips: The scholarship is administered by the OAS Academic Program and delivered by Universidad de los Andes (UDD), so read the announcement on the OAS site rather than on UDD's site for the routing rules.
Because the award is partial by design, budget the remaining USD 400 of the course yourself before applying.
application_tips: Send the résumé and one letter of recommendation by the deadline of January 31; the announcement names email delivery to the UDD scholarships address, so keep a record of what you sent.
Make the résumé carry data-specific evidence (courses, projects, tools) rather than general employment history, since the scholarship is for a data literacy course.
Have your letter of recommendation written by someone who can speak to your reasoning with data specifically, not just your general performance.
The course is delivered online over four months of lectures, so you can apply from anywhere without relocating - but you must still meet the course cadence.
documents: Résumé
One letter of recommendation
mistakes_to_avoid: Treating the award as covering the full course cost; USD 400 remains payable by you.
Submitting a generic recommendation letter that says nothing about your data work.
Missing the January 31 deadline; the announcement does not publish a grace period.
Applying for a degree programme: this award is only for the 2GL online course, not for a UDD degree.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: Deadline: January 31 as published in the announcement (no year given). Send the résumé and letter of recommendation to the UDD scholarships address before that date.

records.description: AGCID (Agencia Chilena de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo) finances master's degree studies in Chile for foreign professionals, covering the total cost of tuition (matrícula), tuition fees (arancel) and titling for the full duration of studies, up to a maximum of 24 months. Every scholarship includes a monthly maintenance payment of CLP 600,000 for candidates who study in person or hybrid, insurance for those staying in Chile, CLP 90,000 for texts and materials and CLP 300,000 of thesis support, while travel costs, personal expenses and airfare are not funded. Courses must begin between 1 March and 30 September 2027 and finish by 28 February 2029, and Spanish is the working language of instruction.

eligibility: Chilean professionals resident in Colombia who do NOT have a higher-education degree issued in Chile (this call is administered by ICETEX as focal point)
Technical, technological and professional graduates who can present a postgraduate specialisation
Minimum 55 base points in the call's evaluation system
benefits: Financing is for the full duration of studies, up to a maximum of 4 semesters or 6 quarters, for a maximum duration of 24 months
Maintenance payment of 600,000 Chilean pesos per month for candidates studying in person or hybrid
Insurance for scholarship holders who remain in Chile
90,000 Chilean pesos for texts, materials and practical activities required by the studies
300,000 Chilean pesos of thesis support, delivered in full at the end of studies for those who complete the required work
Financing for academic, cultural, social, sporting or professional enrichment activities linked to the studies at the host university
The airfare, city transportation, personal expenses and other expenses NOT covered by the guidelines are NOT financed
Studies can begin between 1 March 2027 and 30 September 2027, and must finish by 28 February 2029
selection_criteria: Preselection by the focal point is made in strict descending order of the qualification, followed by ties broken in descending order by higher academic average (with one decimal rounded up), then by the lowest level of the registro (Grupos Chicos y Medianos)
A total of less than 55 base points in the evaluation does not pass the preselection stage
Chile awards the scholarship based on its own merit criteria
official.application_process: Applications are made through ICETEX as focal point (2027 registration is open at the time of research). Candidates must submit the application on the Anexo forms, the programme of study with the document of the institution's admission or commitment to the candidates or advance subjects, the economic-legal characterisation according to SISBEN, and copies of all the documents listed in the required documents list, all in PDF format in one email. The Comisión Nacional de Becas 2027 will meet on 26 October 2026, and the final results are published from the second half of November 2026 on the AGCID results page using the applicant's identity document number.
key_dates: Extended closing: Thursday 15 October 2026 at 5:00 p.m. (Colombia time)

applicant_utility.description: AGCID covers the whole cost of the degree - 100 percent of matrícula, arancel and titling, up to four semesters or six quarters within a maximum of 24 months - but it does not pay your airfare or your city transport, and it pays monthly maintenance only if you attend in person or hybrid. The working language is Spanish, and the Comisión Nacional de Becas meets on 26 October 2026 with results published from the second half of November.
eligibility_tips: This channel is administered by ICETEX as focal point, and the page addresses Chile-based professionals who do NOT have a higher education degree issued in Chile; candidates in other countries apply through their own focal point's equivalent call.
The threshold is a hard cut-off, not a guideline: the page states that a total of less than 55 base points in the evaluation does not pass the preselection stage.
Check the language of instruction before applying. The programme is administered in Spanish, and no English language requirement is published - your coursework will be in Spanish.
application_tips: Watch for extensions: the deadline was moved from the initial 9 October 2026 at 1:00 p.m. to 15 October 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Colombia time, so treat the posted time as firm and submit at least a day early.
Send everything in one email, all in PDF, with the SISBEN characterisation and the study-programme document included; the ICETEX page makes that format a requirement, not a preference.
Include the programme of study document with the copy of the requirements required by your destination programme, since it is one of the Anexes that is explicitly listed.

Understand the scoring before you apply: a total below 55 base points fails preselection, and ties are broken by higher academic average (rounded up to one decimal) and then by the lowest level of the registro, so your weighted average matters at the margin.
Because monitoring is per the guidelines, keep the original mailing receipts and the submission confirmation email.

mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming 100 percent of the cost of the degree means 100 percent of your living costs: airfare, city transport and personal expenses are explicitly not financed.
Applying for a virtual or fully online programme: the monthly maintenance payment is only for in-person or hybrid study.
Sending documents piecemeal or in another format: the ICETEX page requires everything in PDF in one email.
Falling below 55 base points in the evaluation, which ends the journey at preselection.
Missing the extended deadline: the initial closing of 9 October 2026 was moved to 15 October 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Colombia time.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: Deadline: 15 October 2026, 5:00 p.m. Colombia time (extended from 9 October 2026, 1:00 p.m.). The Comisión Nacional de Becas meets on 26 October 2026 and results are posted from the second half of November 2026 on the AGCID results page.
